public_prompt: A warehouse robot's onboard sensor emits three acceleration channels. The team's framing is: integrate the first two channels twice to recover the path over the floor. The recovered path walks into the racking. Report the corrected path computation.
observable_resources: robot/imu.csv — 180,000 rows of ax, ay, az plus a heading column in degrees that swings up to 90 degrees per second during turns
robot/recovered-path.csv — the current integration; agrees with the surveyed marks along straight aisle runs and diverges by up to 6 m immediately after every turn
robot/ground-truth.csv — 42 crossings of surveyed floor marks with exact positions
robot/sensor-datasheet.md — the three channels report proper acceleration along the chassis forward, lateral and vertical directions
closure:navigation-tuning-v7 — closed; raises the drift correction gain to mask the post-turn divergence
closure:robot-safety-certification — closed; certifies the chassis on stopping distance and guarding; rests on physical tests, not on any recovered track
closure:aisle-marking-standard — closed; fixes the floor markings and their spacing; rests on the warehouse standard, not on how the track is recovered

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the acceleration channels are rotated into the floor's fixed reference using the heading at each sample before integrating, and the answer explains why the error appears strictly after turns — the chassis directions and the floor directions agree on straight runs and disagree afterwards. FAIL if the answer raises the correction gain, low-pass filters the channels, blames sensor bias, or adds more surveyed marks.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the direct-integration framing tunes the drift gain, which fits the straight runs and leaves the post-turn 6 m error intact.
